---
title: "1: PBMC preprocessing"
output: html_notebook
---

In this notebook, we perform preprocessing and QC on our PBMC CITE-seq data. Multimodal clustering and cell type annotation are performed in a follow-up notebook, 2_pbmc_cell_type_annotation.Rmd. 

Note 11/10/26: Previously, libraries for the healthy controls and subject 594 were mislabeled (i.e. they were swapped with one another). This issue has been corrected. Corrected files are marked with an _r.

First, clear the environment and set the path where the project folder is saved.

```{r}
# Clear all objects from environment
rm(list = ls(all.names = TRUE))
# Free up memory
gc()
# Increase max vector memory
mem.maxVSize(200000)

project_path <- "/Users/juliaelrod/Desktop/cmu/research/scleroderma/jSSc_ASCT_monocytes_manuscript/code_for_manuscript/"
```

Now load in useful packages and custom functions.

```{r}
# Load packages
packages <- c("Seurat", "dplyr", "tidyr", "SeuratDisk", "harmony", "readr",
              "ggplot2", "stringr", "SoupX", "dsb", "data.table", "Matrix",
              "scDblFinder", "scater")
invisible(lapply(packages, require, character.only = TRUE))

# Source functions
function_files <- list.files(paste0(project_path, "functions"), pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)
invisible(lapply(function_files, source))
```

Now, we prepare a Seurat object with one counts matrix for all samples, as well as all necessary metadata.

Prior to preprocessing, we have 44,706 cells total. The sample for patient 515 at 12 months is missing due to quality issues.

Due to a previous problem we had with mislabeled samples, we check to make sure that expression of sex-linked genes is consistent with our demographic information.

```{r}
scler_pbmc_r <- LoadH5Seurat(paste0(project_path, "data/h5seurat/scler_pbmc_r_1.h5seurat"))

# First check that sex-linked genes expression is correct.
# All samples from 515, as well as H3 should express Y linked genes
# All samples from 591 and 594, as well as H1, H2, and  H4 should express X linked gene XIST
sex_dotplot <- DotPlot(scler_pbmc_r,
                       features = c("XIST", # X-linked
                                    "RPS4Y1", # Y-linked
                                    "DDX3Y", # Y-linked
                                    "KDM5D", # Y-linked
                                    "EIF1AY", # Y-linked
                                    "UTY", # Y-linked
                                    "ZFY"), # Y-linked
                       group.by = "sample_id",
                       dot.scale = 10)

# Color dots by the recorded sex of each sample (pink = female, blue = male), so a
# mismatch between recorded sex and sex-linked gene expression stands out.
# Transparency shows scaled average expression; size shows percent expressed.
dot_data <- sex_dotplot$data
sample_sex <- scler_pbmc_r@meta.data %>% distinct(sample_id, sex)
dot_data$sex <- sample_sex$sex[match(dot_data$id, sample_sex$sample_id)]

ggplot(dot_data, aes(x = features.plot, y = id,
                     size = pct.exp, colour = sex, alpha = avg.exp.scaled)) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_radius(range = c(0, 10), name = "Percent Expressed") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(F = "hotpink", M = "dodgerblue"),
                      labels = c(F = "Female", M = "Male"),
                      name = "Sex") +
  scale_alpha(range = c(0.15, 1), name = "Average Expression") +
  labs(x = "Features", y = "sample_id") +
  cowplot::theme_cowplot() +
  coord_flip() +
  RotatedAxis()
```

Now, we begin preprocessing

1) Multimodal multiplet detection with COMPOSITE.

First, we extract the RNA and ADT counts matrices, filter out genes with > 50% zeroes, and save both matrices as mtx files.


Composite is implemented in Python in the file, composite_pbmc.py.

See https://github.com/CHPGenetics/COMPOSITE

We import the multiplet predictions as a CSV file.

We detect 10,568 multiplets (23.6%).

After removing multiplets, 34,138 cells remain.

3) Quality control based on RNA and ADT features

After this filtering step, we retain 29,806 cells.

6) Denoise and normalize ADT data

Now, let's denoise and normalize the ADT data with DSB. We set denoise.counts = FALSE since our signal is weak and our ADT data is not bimodal. We also scale the data. 

For this step, we use the output from cellranger multi without demultiplexing (as we did when we ran SoupX for the ambient RNA correction).

7) Batch integration

Now, we integrate the RNA data using harmony and the ADT data using RPCA to account for batch effects.

```{r}
scler_pbmc_r <- LoadH5Seurat(paste0(project_path, "data/h5seurat/scler_pbmc_r_7.h5seurat"))

# Data integration

# (1) RNA - Run Harmony
# Set default assay
DefaultAssay(scler_pbmc_r) <- "RNA"
# Run PCA
scler_pbmc_r <- RunPCA(scler_pbmc_r, reduction.name = "pca_rna")
# Set dimensions
rna_dims <- 1:30
# Integrate with harmony
scler_pbmc_r <- RunHarmony(scler_pbmc_r, group.by.vars = "LIBRARY", reduction.use = "pca_rna", dims.use = rna_dims, verbose = TRUE)

# (2) ADT - Run RPCA
# Set default assay
DefaultAssay(scler_pbmc_r) <- "DSB"
# Integrate with RPCA (Seurat integration)
scler_pbmc_r <- run_rpca(scler_pbmc_r)

# Save integrated Seurat object
SaveH5Seurat(scler_pbmc_r, paste0(project_path, "data/h5seurat/scler_pbmc_r_8"))
```
